newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF REAL MADRID PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF REAL MADRID PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of the Real Madrid players most likely to feature against Real Betis in the Spanish league championship game on Saturday:

Bodo Illgner, goalkeeper, 29. A surprise signing at the beginning of the season after coach Fabio Capello demanded a taller 'keeper, the former German international has become one of the mainstays of the Real side since ousting Canizares and veteran Paco Buyo.

Santiago Canizares, goalkeeper, 27. Shot to prominence after keeping Spain's World Cup hopes alive against Denmark in 1993, Canizares is anxious to move on after playing second fiddle to Buyo and then to Illgner since joining Real from Celta Vigo.
Rafael Alkorta, defender, 28. A regular in the national side and ever-present at the heart of the Real defence this season, Alkorta is one of the toughest markers in Spain.

Fernando Hierro, defender, 28. The tower on which the Real defence is built, Hierro comes forward well and is strong in the air at set pieces. A potentially lethal free-kick specialist, Hierro has scored two superb goals in the past few weeks.
Chendo Porlan, defender 35. Veteran defender who has been playing for Real since 1983. Chendo is an unlikely starter but always a reliable substitute.

Roberto Carlos, defender, 23. Quick in turning defence into attack down the left, the Brazilian international is a fine corner taker and has a devastating shot at set pieces. Drilled home a 30-metre free kick against Betis in September.

Christian Panucci, defender, 23. Has slotted straight into the Real line-up since making his debut on the right of defence after signing from AC Milan for around 700 million pesetas ($5.34 million) last month. Dangerous at Roberto Carlos corners.
Fernando Sanz, defender, 23. Substitute defender who is still trying to escape the shadow of being the son of Real president Lorenzo Sanz.
Luis Milla, midfielder, 30. Milla's signing from Barcelona sent shockwaves through the Spanish game back in 1990 but he has since fallen from favour and is an unlikely starter.
Manuel Sanchis, midfielder, 31. Son of a 1960s Real star, Sanchis had been a regular first-team choice in both defence and midfield since 1983 but has struggled to impress Capello.
Fernando Redondo, midfielder, 27. Argentine international with a delicate touch, the injury-prone Redondo is yet to find his form this season after missing seven months' league action.

Clarence Seedorf, midfielder, 20. Dutch international whose busy support work behind the frontmen has made him an unsung hero since signing from Ajax in the close season. Scored a fine goal last week against Hercules.

Victor Sanchez, midfielder, 20. Quietly efficient midfielder whose work down the right has earnt him promotion from Real's B team. Played superb games against Barcelona and Atletico but likely to be kept on the bench in favour of Amavisca.
Emilio Amavisca, midfielder/striker, 25. A skilful support player rather than goalscorer, the Spanish international has recently returned after missing several months through injury.

Raul Gonzalez, midfielder/striker, 19. Extraordinarily mature 19-year-old who continues to improve despite playing out of position after being moved back to the left side of midfield with the arrival of Suker and Mijatovic. A true match-winner.

Davor Suker, striker, 29. With 16 goals already this season the Croatian Euro 96 star has continued to shine since signing from Sevilla. Heavily left-sided, Suker can take on men and beat them before unleashing a powerful shot. Strong at set pieces.

Predrag Mijatovic, striker, 27. The Montenegrin's lethal right foot made him Spain's second-highest goalscorer at Valencia last season. Has moved into attack after starting in midfield. Frequently accused of diving in the penalty area.
